target.title: docs(gateway): add reply session init conflict troubleshooting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators hitting `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>` currently have no troubleshooting entry to consult. The error string is opaque, and the actual root cause — two concurrent gateway processes sharing one data directory / contending for one port — is not discoverable from the message alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a new section to `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md` covering the root cause and recovery steps for this error. The conflict is an optimistic-concurrency `stale-snapshot` rejection in the session store, triggered when more than one gateway process binds the same port and locks the same data directory (e.g. an orphaned process plus a `KeepAlive`-managed one, or a redundant second supervisor job such as a left-over `ai.hermes.gateway`).

The section documents how to:
- identify concurrent processes/PIDs and lock-file ownership,
- disable the redundant supervisor job (bootout + disable its plist),
- kill any orphan holding the port,
- restart the canonical job and verify a single `LISTEN`, a single PID, and that the running PID matches the lock-file PID.

This is purely additive (`docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`, +75 / −0) and slots in before the existing macOS stability section.

## User Impact

Operators can self-diagnose and recover from this error without filing an issue. No runtime, config, or code surface changes — documentation only.

## Evidence

- Diff: `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md` only, `75 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.
- Verified the live scenario this documents: after disabling the redundant job and removing the orphan, the gateway runs as a single stable instance — one `LISTEN` on its port, exactly one gateway PID, and the running PID matches the lock-file PID.
- `git diff --check` clean; no whitespace errors.

Co-Authored-By: Oz <oz-agent@warp.dev>
---

## Related

- #98416 — open tracker for `reply session initialization conflicted` on `2026.6.11` (published-dist reentrancy-guard defect). This PR does **not** fix that defect; it documents a distinct **operational** cause — two concurrent gateway processes (e.g. an orphaned process or a redundant second supervisor job such as a left-over `ai.hermes.gateway`) sharing one data directory and contending for one port — that operators observing this error should rule out during triage.
